events.title: New Orleans Is Founded
events.description: Jean-Baptiste Le Moyne de Bienville, working for the Mississippi Company, founded a French colonial settlement on a bend of the Mississippi River. He named it after Philippe II, Duke of Orléans, who was then regent of France.
events.significance: The settlement grew into one of North America's most important port cities and a distinctive cultural crossroads. Its location controlled access to the Mississippi's mouth.

events.title: Beethoven's Ninth Symphony Premieres
events.description: In Vienna, Ludwig van Beethoven's Ninth Symphony debuted. The composer was almost completely deaf and stood on stage beside the conductor. The work ends with a choral setting of Schiller's 'Ode to Joy'.
events.significance: It was the first major symphony to include voices. It is regarded as one of the greatest works in Western music, and its 'Ode to Joy' theme later became the anthem of the European Union.

events.title: RMS Lusitania Sunk by a German U-Boat
events.description: The British ocean liner Lusitania was torpedoed by the German submarine U-20 off the southern coast of Ireland and sank in about 18 minutes. Nearly 1,200 people died, including many civilians and over 100 Americans.
events.significance: The sinking turned public opinion in many countries against Germany. It also strained relations between Germany and the United States, which entered World War I in 1917.

events.title: Germany Signs Unconditional Surrender
events.description: At Allied headquarters in Reims, France, German representatives signed the act of military surrender, bringing the war in Europe to an end. The surrender took effect the next day, which was celebrated as V-E Day.
events.significance: The surrender ended the Nazi regime's war in Europe after nearly six years of fighting. It marked a turning point in 20th-century history.
